title: How much juice does each friend drink?
description: Four friends share three glasses of sugarcane juice equally. Each glass is cut into four equal parts, each friend takes one part from every glass, and the parts are counted back to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a few wholes are shared equally, cut every whole into equal parts and give each person one part from each. Watch for students who write three or four as the share, or who forget that the share is more than one fourth.

source: Four friends ordered 3 glasses of sugarcane juice and shared it equally among themselves. Each one drank ____ glass of sugarcane juice.
video_script.why: The child shares three glasses equally among four friends by cutting each glass into four equal parts, and names one friend's share as a fraction.
video_script.substitution: Treat each glass as one roti cut into four equal parts, and give each friend one part from every roti.
video_script.anchor: Four friends sharing three glasses of sugarcane juice equally
video_script.payoff_line: Each friend drinks three fourths of a glass
maths_rules: each of the 3 glasses is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 1/4 glass
each friend takes one part from every glass, so 3 parts of 1/4 glass each
3 x 1/4 = 3/4, so each friend drinks 3/4 glass
check: 4 friends x 3 parts = 12 parts, and 3 glasses x 4 parts = 12 parts
video_script.design: One idea: three wholes shared among four, cut every whole into four and give each person one part from each. Same method as sharing one roti. The four friends and the three glasses stay on the board to the end.
